data.title: Australia's Jobless Rate Rises to Highest Level Since 2021 — Update
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--Australia's unemployment rate jumped in October to its highest level since late 2021, highlighting fears that the economy is slowing rapidly due to weak confidence and five interest-rate increases since the start of the year.

Unemployment hit 4.9% in October, up from 4.7% in September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Thursday.

The economy lost 43,500 jobs in October, with part-time employment falling by 40,600.

Higher unemployment will argue strongly for the Reserve Bank of Australia to keep interest rates on hold from here, albeit data on Wednesday showed wages grew at their fastest pace since 2023 in the third quarter.

RBA Gov. Michele Bullock also affirmed this week her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Inflation data for October will be released next week, with economists warning that there is a high risk that it will once again surprise on the high side of estimates.

Still, the impact of interest-rate increases this year is becoming increasingly obvious, with lending for new homes collapsing and house prices heading toward record losses.

The RBA has talked about the difficult policy task before, highlighting that elevated inflation remains its main priority.

The bank recently forecast that inflation will remain above target until mid-2028, amid concerns inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

"With the labor market continuing to weaken rapidly, we remain comfortable in our view that the RBA won't tighten policy any further," said Abhijit Surya, senior economist at Capital Economics.

The employment-to-population ratio fell 0.3 percentage point to 63.3%, and the participation rate fell 0.2 percentage point to 66.6%

The number of hours worked fell 0.2% in October, while the underemployment rate fell 0.1 percentage point to 6.2%.

The Australian dollar fell on the data to 66.90 U.S. cents from around 67.20 U.S. cents.

Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: Gold And Silver Are Getting Crushed: Analysts Split As Precious Metals Lose $3.3 Trillion In Market Value
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold and silver are now trading at their lowest level since September 2025.
  • Economist Peter Schiff dismissed concerns about gold and silver prices, noting that the metals are likely to hold much better than other assets in the long term. 
  • Analyst Michaël van de Poppe noted that gold's slip was not a surprise after its “massive” upward shock at the end of last year. 

The precious metals trade took a hit on Wednesday after the dollar surged to its highest level since April 2025 and the Federal Reserve minutes flagged inflation concerns.

Spot gold prices slipped below $3,750 an ounce, while silver plunged below $45 an ounce. Gold and silver are now trading at their lowest level since September 2025. Platinum and palladium prices also fell.

However, bulls said precious metals are still a long-term hold, while critics were concerned prices could plunge further.

Metals Bull Sees A Long-Term Hold In Gold, Silver Amid Growing Market Volatility 

Economist Peter Schiff dismissed concerns about gold and silver prices, noting that the metals are likely to hold much better than other assets in the long term.

In a post on X, he said, “Investors act as if the only collateral damage in the Fed's inflation war will be gold and silver. But precious metals will ultimately hold up much better than stocks, real estate, banks, or the U.S. economy, and then get a much bigger boost from the ensuing inflationary bailout.”

The Fed minutes pointed to broad-based inflation pressures in the economy, adding that they warrant action, with some policymakers advocating a larger rate hike in upcoming meetings.

Critics Think Precious Metals Have Not Yet Bottomed

Analyst Michaël van de Poppe noted that gold slipping was not a surprise following its “massive” upward shock at the end of last year. “No wonder it has to come down and I don't think it's done. I expect to see some bounces on the way, and this is definitely an area where it could happen (or $3,200), but I'm not looking to buy Gold in my long-term portfolio. I'd wait. Times will come,” he said in a post on X.

Veteran trader Peter L Brandt said in a post on X, “Once Silver bottoms it could take many quarters, even years, to build a base.”

As per Bitcoin Archive, gold and silver’s 10% drop over the last nine days have wiped out $3.3 trillion in market value. This is larger than Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) over $1 trillion loss since CEO Jensen Huang’s infidelity reports and subsequent resignation from the company.

What’s Retail Saying About Gold, Silver?

The SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD), which tracks the price of gold, closed down nearly 3% lower on Wednesday but recovered some of its losses overnight.

Retail sentiment around GLD jumped from ‘bearish’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours on Stocktwits.

One user said, “$GLD will settle around $200-$220 !! Still a Lot of inflationary froth to melt.” GLD last closed at $341.19.

However, another bullish user said, “$GLD almost. It should start reversing here.”

Meanwhile, the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) plunged more than 4.5% at close on Wednesday but also reversed to green in the overnight session.

Retail sentiment around SLV improved from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours.

One user said, “$PALL $SLV good time to add. When market corrects harder these will be safe havens.”

However, another user said, “$SLV This thing is in complete free fall, unbelievable.”

GLD is down nearly 14% year-to-date, while SLV has plunged nearly 37% in the same time.

data.title: Australia's Jobless Jump Could Be Pivotal Moment for Rates — Market Talk
data.description: The unexpected jump in Australia's unemployment in October to 4.9% could prove to be a pivotal moment in the Australian interest rates cycle, says Krishna Bhimavarapu, APAC economist at State Street Investment Management. After months in which the impact of higher interest rates was most visible in housing, confidence and other interest-rate-sensitive sectors, the slowdown is now showing up clearly in the labor market, he adds. The data are beginning to reflect the cumulative impact of the substantial policy tightening delivered to date, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.title: Asian markets mixed as investors weigh Anthropic's record IPO against Fed rate hike risks
data.description:
Asian equities traded mixed on Thursday November 19, as investors weighed Anthropic's record initial public offering against a sharp selloff in commodities and the prospect of further US interest-rate rises.

Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.55%, after opening little changed. The broader Topix slipped 0.26%. Hang Seng futures lost 0.5%.

South Korea's market will open for regular trading at 10 am local time instead of 9 am, and will close at 4:30 pm, an hour later than usual today on account of the country's 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test, known as Suneung.

The change eases morning traffic so students can reach their college entrance exam centres on time. Authorities also asked government offices and businesses to start later.

In India, the GIFT Nifty which indicates how the country's stock market could open for the day's trade implied at a gap down at open.

In currency markets, the Japanese yen held at 159.42 per dollar, and the offshore yuan stood at 6.6681.

US equity-index futures rose as Nasdaq 100 contracts climbed 0.9% and S&P 500 contracts added 0.5%. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the marketed range, in the largest first-time share sale on record. It is also the first listing by a frontier AI lab. US Treasuries meanwhile rose for a third day.

The offering will test investor appetite for technology stocks after recent losses. Nvidia, a key gauge of the AI trade, has tumbled in recent weeks after Jensen Huang's ouster and growing fears that AI spending may slow. Anthropic's debut also puts it ahead of OpenAI, which does not plan to list before 2027.

According to a regulatory filing on Thursday, Anthropic raised about $3 billion there by selling 36.1 million Class A shares. That sat at the low end of its target. It had expected to sell 38.5 million to 50 million shares and raise $3 billion to $3.5 billion.

Japan is one of the few places where household buyers had direct access to the IPO as per a Bloomberg report.

The Fed's October minutes showed nearly all officials expected to raise rates "in the months ahead" to bring inflation back to 2%. Two policymakers said a move larger than 25 basis points could be justified in December if inflation data disappointed according to a Bloomberg report.

San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly urged a measured approach, while Governor Michael Barr said higher borrowing costs would likely be appropriate, the report noted.

Oil prices, meanwhile, steadied on Thursday, after a sharp slide in the previous session, as traders weighed what comes next in the US-Iran conflict. Brent crude traded at $91.43 a barrel in early Asian trade, having closed below $92 on Wednesday. West Texas Intermediate held near $83 a barrel after it lost 3.2% in the midweek session.

data.title: Copper Rises on Potential Technical Rebound — Market Talk
data.description: Copper rises in early Asia trade, after tumbling to its lowest level in seven months in the previous session. The metal is one of the beneficiaries of the artificial-intelligence investment boom, ANZ Research analysts say in a note. The rapid expansion of data centers, along with the generation and grid infrastructure needed to power them, has shifted expectations for copper consumption. However, a wave of selling hit commodity markets recently, as risk appetite was weighed by concerns that this year's AI-related rally across equity markets has been overdone, they add. The three-month copper futures contract on the London Metal Exchange rises 1.5% to $12,661.00 a metric ton. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
